text.p: Hungary's Rita Kovacs triumphed in the 25-kilometre river marathon and Alexei Akatiev retained his five-kilometre crown to complete a golden Russian treble at the European swimming championships on Friday.

The imperturbable Kovacs allowed leading rival Valeria Casprini to build up a three-minute lead before overhauling the 21-year-old Italian on the 23rd kilometre to win the gold by 90 seconds in a 5-1/2-hour epic in the River Guadalquivir.
That battle unfolded from the early morning light to the blazing heat of early afternoon over five laps of a 5-km circuit.

Akatiev beat fellow Russian Yevgeny Bezruchenko in a much closer race over one lap of the same stretch of water in the early evening to keep the five-km title he won with more than a minute to spare at the 1995 championships in Vienna.

Akatiev won in the 56 minutes and seven seconds -- seven seconds clear of Bezruchenko and 12 ahead of bronze medallist Luca Baldini of Italy, who foiled a Russian medal sweep by finishing a mere second before Alexei Stepanov.
The win capped a great day for Russia, who had earlier celebrated two more repeat victories for synchronised swimmer Olga Sedakova and diver Vera Ilyina in the San Pablo pool complex.
Sedakova claimed the European solo crown for the fourth successive time, surpassing the treble achieved by Britain's Carolyn Wilson in the 1980s.
She picked up four perfect 10.0 marks in the process, amassed 99.240 points and won comfortably from Virginie Dedieu of France and Giovanna Burlando of Italy.
Ilyina drew on her equally vast experience to snatch victory with her fifth and last dive and retain her one-metre springboard title.
Ilyina, world three-metre silver medallist, overtook German Doerte Lindner with her fifth and last effort to hoist her European medal tally to three golds, two silvers and one bronze.
Compatriot Irina Lashko, an equally seasoned competitor, pipped Lindner for the silver with the last dive of the final.
Across town, world silver medallist Kovacs did not even look out of breath at the end of a 25-km race in which she maintained a metronomically steady pace her rivals could not match.

Three of the 17 starters -- leading Czech contender Yvetta Hlavacova and Britons Sara Ward and Alix Scott -- could not complete the gruelling event which world swimming's governing body wants included in the Olympics.
Kovacs, third for much of the race, caught 1995 silver medallist Edith van Dijk on the fourth lap and passed the brave Casprini halfway through the last.
"I thought it was so fast at the beginning. I thought it was too fast for the 25 kilometres but I trusted myself," Kovacs said.
"During the race I was really tired but my mind was strong."
Kovacs, European five-km champion in 1995, won in five hours 21 minutes 58 seconds, with Casprini second in 5:23.28 and Van Dijk third in 5:25:28.
